issues.description: The problem statement and template expect concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (used in the UML and in Main.java), but the solution repository implements these as SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead and leaves Goat.java/Pig.java/Seal.java effectively empty. This naming/type mismatch between the expected class names and the solution's class names is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which class names to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution repository use the same animal class names as the problem statement and template (Seal, Pig, Goat) — either by renaming SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat to Seal/Pig/Goat or by providing concrete Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java implementations that match the expected API. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to accept the Space-prefixed class names consistently. Ensure Main.java and the UML refer to the same class names.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (and the Main.java in the template references Seal, Pig, Goat), but the provided reference implementation uses SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This divergence means students trying to map the assignment description and template to the solution (or vice versa) will encounter differently named classes for the same conceptual entities, creating confusion about which classes to implement or use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the names across artifacts: either rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat (and keep their implementations), or update the problem statement and template to refer to SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat consistently. Preferably rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat so they directly match the UML, tasks, and template Main.java.
